analysis:
The PR changes .github/workflows/release-provider.yml only, in two places: a comment edit at head lines 181-182 and a new job-level env block in qualify-sdk (head lines 239-242) setting DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT: prod. It is a static literal. It adds no secrets and no new expression interpolation, and no permissions or triggers change.

Security effect: qualify-sdk (base lines 230-250) runs the lane: qualification action with read-only contents permission, and it feeds no signing or publish step. Artifacts are built in build-provider, which still receives the resolved environment (base line 182, unchanged). The signing job (build-and-release) still checks the final runtime-smoke output for build-environment ${ENV_PREFIX} (base lines 561 and 848). It also verifies the CLI name and the production designated requirement. So the prod pin cannot make a dev or staging artifact appear to be a prod artifact.

The change makes the SDK-27 qualification tests see production identity defaults on the dev branch. That is a correctness fix for test fidelity. One residual: the qualification action's own `environment` input (base line 250) is still the resolved environment. How the composite action combines that input with the job-level env var is not visible. The effect is limited to test and qualification context, and I see no credential or trust-boundary impact.

No threat-model items are affected. T-034 and T-054 govern official-build identity, and they are enforced at signing and registration, which this PR does not touch. No findings.
